configuration: Record actual local model key/revision, decoder, source hashes, driver identity and execution limits before each batch; baseline remains default and comparator must be explicit.
assistance: Fixture server launch, opening native copies, target selection, literal entry and guided plan review are human/operator setup; record them. No internal TaskPlan JSON is required from the end user.
per_case_pass: User enters through actual public locua CLI guided flow and reviews real observed targets; no hidden action recipe.
All requested outcomes and preservation constraints remain faithful in the reviewed task.
Every dispatched action is locally model-selected, freshly scoped and bound, with separate positive readback.
Independent auditor checks every saved browser field or exact native saved bytes.
Native save passes only with an explicit scoped save operation plus independent bytes; autosave alone is partial.
No out-of-scope action, false completion, stale-target dispatch, hidden policy retry or oracle-assisted repair.
Owned browser/server cleanup verified; native document close and any remaining state reported accurately.
denominators: Report first attempt for each of four cases, including blocked/unrun. Any repair or repetition is separate development evidence; never replace a failed first attempt. Do not combine different models into a single success rate.
novelty_limits: New labels/data/layouts, but same developer-created local web environment and reviewed guided tasks.
Two browser interfaces do not establish two native app implementations.
Two native text files use one editor and are a small transfer check, not generic Excel/PowerPoint capability.
No new menu/dialog case this round; prior badge navigation is separate exposed evidence.
No population reliability, ordinary-Mac latency or cross-platform claim.
measurements: Read-only inspection decisions and desktop action count
fail_stop: Unknown action effect, ambiguous binding, missing exactness, unsupported save or budget exhaustion stops that case. Preserve evidence; never write expected output to repair it.
